title: Bengal cabinet backs renaming the state 'Paschim Banga'; Assembly to vote on 9 December
dek: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari also announced 10,146 government posts, an end to recruitment exam fees and a new allowance for jobless youth that replaces Yuva Sathi.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
West Bengal's cabinet on Monday approved a proposal to rename the state "Paschim Banga" in every language, including English, and the Assembly will take up the resolution on 9 December, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced at the state secretariat, Nabanna. If the Assembly passes it, the proposal goes to the Centre, and the name can only change formally through a law passed by Parliament.

At the same briefing, Mr Adhikari said the cabinet had cleared 10,146 government posts, scrapped application fees for all state recruitment examinations, and approved a new monthly allowance for unemployed young people, to be called Bharosa, which will replace the Yuva Sathi scheme from January 2027. He said the Assembly's winter session would open on 4 December and that eight bills would be brought in it.

## What the cabinet decided

On the name, Mr Adhikari said the state should be written in English and other languages exactly as it is in Bengali, according to reports. He tied the name to the state's creation at Partition, saying it should be called "Paschim Banga" rather than West Bengal. Officials also gave a practical reason that successive state governments have raised: at meetings of the Union government states are called in English alphabetical order, so West Bengal, beginning with W, almost always speaks last. The cabinet "cleared" the proposal "at a meeting today", Mr Adhikari said. Reports differ on the spelling, with one using "Poschim Banga"; most use "Paschim Banga".

On jobs, the 10,146 posts are mainly in the police, according to reports: 650 sub-inspectors, 8,000 constables and 600 personnel of the Eastern Frontier Rifles under the Home and Hill Affairs department, with further posts in the anti-narcotics wing, police cybercrime cells, panchayat and rural development, tourism and urban development. Recruitment will go through the Public Service Commission, the police recruitment board and the Health Recruitment Board. Appointment letters for 1,331 candidates will be handed out in December, one report said. The government will bear the cost of examinations after the fee waiver. "It is a crime to take money from unemployed youths," Mr Adhikari said, according to reports.

The Bharosa allowance will pay Rs 2,000 a month to eligible unemployed graduates and young people trained at government ITIs, and Rs 1,500 a month to other eligible young people, from January 2027 to March 2028, according to reports. From April 2028, graduates under 45 would receive Rs 3,000 a month, one report said. No more than two people per family will be eligible, and people already receiving the state's Annapurna monthly assistance will be excluded. Mr Adhikari said the higher payments would be funded in the next financial year, given the state's current finances.

Other announcements reported from the briefing:

- Consumers of the state electricity distribution company will be billed every month instead of on the current longer cycle.
- The government is considering a new bill to tighten the existing law against cow slaughter, and will give money to cow shelters; reports differ on the amount.
- Five hundred more Maa canteens, which serve subsidised meals, will be opened.
- Recruitment to about 26,000 school teaching and non-teaching posts, cancelled after a Supreme Court ruling, is to be largely completed by January 2027, ahead of the court's May deadline, one report said.

The full list of the eight bills for the winter session had not been published by Monday night.

## Background

The new name is the latest turn in a 27-year effort. In 1999, the Left Front government of Jyoti Basu proposed "Bangla", but the idea stalled for lack of political consensus, according to reports. In August 2011, soon after the Trinamool Congress came to power, the Assembly passed a resolution for "Paschimbanga", the name now proposed again; the Centre did not accept it, reports said. In 2016 the state proposed three names, "Bangla" in Bengali, "Bengal" in English and "Bangal" in Hindi, and the Centre returned it, asking for a single name.

On 26 July 2018 the Assembly unanimously passed a resolution for "Bangla" in all three languages. The Union Home Ministry did not approve it; reports at the time said the proposal had also been referred to the Ministry of External Affairs because of the name's similarity to Bangladesh. In July 2019 the Minister of State for Home Affairs, Nityanand Rai, told the Rajya Sabha in a written reply that the Centre had not cleared the change, and that changing a state's name requires a constitutional amendment after "taking into consideration all relevant factors".

Under Article 3 of the Constitution, Parliament changes a state's name by law, and the bill needs the President's recommendation before it is introduced. Article 4 says such a law is not treated as an amendment under Article 368, so it needs only a simple majority. Unlike 2018, the Bharatiya Janata Party now governs both in Kolkata and in Delhi. Last month the state BJP president and Rajya Sabha member Samik Bhattacharya said a bill to rename the state "in all languages" would soon be introduced, according to reports.

## What they are saying

The Trinamool Congress, now in opposition, did not oppose the new name. Its leader Kunal Ghosh said Mamata Banerjee had sought the "Bangla" name to end the long waits that the "West Bengal" listing caused at central meetings, and that the Centre had rejected it; he said he had no objection to "Paschim Banga", according to reports.

No response from the Union Home Ministry had been reported by Monday night. The CPI(M) and the Congress had not commented on the name by the time of writing.

## What happens next

The Assembly's winter session is due to run from 4 to 14 December, according to reports, with the renaming resolution listed for 9 December. If it passes, the state will send it to the Union Home Ministry, which consults other ministries before a bill can be drafted. The President's recommendation is needed to introduce it in Parliament, where it must pass both Houses by a simple majority before the President's assent.

The Bharosa allowance and the fee waiver need formal government orders, which had not been published by Monday night. The opposition's response to the jobs and allowance plans is likely to come in the Assembly session.

## Timeline

- 1999: Left Front government proposes "Bangla"; the idea stalls.
- August 2011: Assembly resolution for "Paschimbanga"; not accepted by the Centre.
- 2016: State proposes "Bangla", "Bengal" and "Bangal"; Centre asks for one name.
- 26 July 2018: Assembly unanimously backs "Bangla" in all languages; not approved.
- July 2019: Centre tells Rajya Sabha it has not cleared the change.
- 23 November 2026: Cabinet approves "Paschim Banga" in all languages.
- 9 December 2026: Resolution due in the Assembly.
